title: API Rate Limiter
summary: Build an API gateway's rate limiter, then evolve it as traffic patterns and product needs change.

stages.title: Fixed window
stages.requirement:
Let's start simple. Our API gateway needs a rate limiter. Implement
`RateLimiter(limit, window)` with `allow(now) -> bool`, where `now` is an integer
timestamp in seconds (non-decreasing across calls).

Time is split into **fixed windows** `[k*window, (k+1)*window)`. Each window allows at
most `limit` requests: `allow` returns `True` and counts the request, or `False` once
the window's budget is spent. Rejected requests don't count against anything.

```python
rl = RateLimiter(limit=2, window=10)
rl.allow(0)   # True
rl.allow(5)   # True
rl.allow(9)   # False (window [0, 10) is full)
rl.allow(10)  # True  (new window)
```

hiddenTests.name: test_many_requests_same_second
hiddenTests.code:
def test_many_requests_same_second():
    rl = RateLimiter(limit=100, window=1)
    results = [rl.allow(42) for _ in range(150)]
    assert results.count(True) == 100
    assert results[:100] == [True] * 100

hints: Which window does `now` fall in? Integer division gives you a window id.
Remember the current window id and a counter. Reset the counter when the window id changes.

solution.explanation:
`now // window` identifies the fixed window. Keeping just the current window id and a
counter gives O(1) time and O(1) memory. Only accepted requests increment the counter.
The known weakness, worth naming in an interview, is the boundary burst: up to
`2 * limit` requests can pass in a short span straddling two windows.

stages.title: Per-user limits
stages.requirement:
Nice. One global budget means a noisy client starves everyone else. Make limits per user:

- `allow(now, user_id="")`: each `user_id` has its own fixed-window budget. Calls
  without a `user_id` share the `""` bucket, so stage 1 behavior is unchanged.
- `set_limit(user_id, limit)` overrides the default `limit` for one user (e.g. paid tier).
  It applies from the next call on, and the user's current count is kept.

```python
rl = RateLimiter(limit=1, window=60)
rl.set_limit("pro", 3)
rl.allow(0, "free")  # True
rl.allow(1, "free")  # False
rl.allow(2, "pro")   # True (x3 in total)
```

hints: The single counter becomes a counter *per user*.
Map `user_id -> (window_id, count)`, and look up the effective limit as `overrides.get(user_id, default)`.
Default `user_id=""` keeps stage 1 calls working unchanged.

solution.explanation:
The window-and-counter pair becomes per-user state in a dict, and the limit is
resolved per call from an override map. Defaulting `user_id` to `""` makes the old
single-bucket behavior a special case, so stage 1 tests still pass. Memory now grows
with active users. In production you'd evict idle users or keep this state in Redis.

stages.title: Sliding window
stages.requirement:
Customers are gaming the window boundaries, sending `limit` requests at 0:59 and `limit`
more at 1:00. Add a mode:

- `RateLimiter(limit, window, mode="fixed")`. The default `"fixed"` keeps today's behavior.
- With `mode="sliding"`, a request at `now` is allowed if the user had fewer than their
  limit **accepted** requests in the last `window` seconds, i.e. with timestamps in
  `(now - window, now]`.
- Any other mode raises `ValueError`. Per-user limits apply in both modes.

```python
rl = RateLimiter(limit=2, window=10, mode="sliding")
rl.allow(0); rl.allow(9)   # True, True
rl.allow(10)               # True  (the request at 0 is now outside (0, 10])
rl.allow(11)               # False (9 and 10 are inside (1, 11])
```

hiddenTests.name: test_sliding_scale
hiddenTests.description: Twice the allowed rate for a long stretch: exactly half gets through.
hiddenTests.code:
def test_sliding_scale():
    rl = RateLimiter(limit=1000, window=100, mode="sliding")
    # 20 requests/second for 10,000 seconds against a 10/second budget.
    accepted = sum(rl.allow(t // 20) for t in range(200_000))
    assert accepted == 100_000

hints: To count requests in `(now - window, now]` you need the timestamps of recent accepted requests, not just a counter.
Keep a deque of accepted timestamps per user. Drop timestamps `<= now - window` from the left, then compare the length with the limit.
Keep both strategies side by side, chosen by `mode`. Fixed mode must behave exactly as before.

solution.explanation:
The sliding log keeps each user's accepted timestamps in a deque. Expired entries are
popped from the left, so each timestamp is pushed and popped once (amortized O(1)),
and the window is exact. The fixed-window path is untouched behind `mode`. The cost is
O(limit) memory per user. If that matters, the sliding-window *counter*
approximation interpolates between two fixed windows.

stages.title: Burst allowance
stages.requirement:
Last one. Mobile clients reconnect in bursts, and product wants to allow short bursts
while keeping the long-run rate. Add `mode="token_bucket"` and a `burst` parameter:
`RateLimiter(limit, window, mode="fixed", burst=0)`.

In token-bucket mode, each user has a bucket with capacity `limit + burst` that **starts
full**. It refills continuously at `limit` tokens per `window` seconds, never above
capacity. A request is allowed if the bucket holds **at least one whole token**, which
it consumes. Rejected requests consume nothing. Per-user `set_limit` changes both the
refill rate and the capacity.

Use exact arithmetic: refill amounts can be fractional (`fractions.Fraction` helps), and
float drift will fail the tests.

```python
rl = RateLimiter(limit=2, window=10, mode="token_bucket", burst=1)
[rl.allow(0) for _ in range(4)]  # [True, True, True, False]  capacity 3
rl.allow(5)                      # True  (refilled 1 token in 5s)
rl.allow(5)                      # False
```

visibleTests.name: test_bucket_example
visibleTests.code:
def test_bucket_example():
    rl = RateLimiter(limit=2, window=10, mode="token_bucket", burst=1)
    assert [rl.allow(0) for _ in range(4)] == [True, True, True, False]
    assert rl.allow(5) is True
    assert rl.allow(5) is False

visibleTests.name: test_refill_caps_at_capacity
visibleTests.code:
def test_refill_caps_at_capacity():
    rl = RateLimiter(limit=1, window=1, mode="token_bucket", burst=2)
    assert [rl.allow(0) for _ in range(3)] == [True] * 3
    assert [rl.allow(1000) for _ in range(4)] == [True, True, True, False]

hiddenTests.name: test_fractional_refill_is_exact
hiddenTests.description: Floating point accumulates error here; 0.1 + 0.9 must be exactly 1.
hiddenTests.code:
def test_fractional_refill_is_exact():
    rl = RateLimiter(limit=3, window=10, mode="token_bucket")
    assert [rl.allow(0) for _ in range(3)] == [True] * 3
    assert rl.allow(3) is False   # 0.9 tokens
    assert rl.allow(4) is True    # 0.9 + 0.3 = 1.2 tokens
    assert rl.allow(7) is True    # 0.2 + 0.9 = 1.1 tokens
    assert rl.allow(10) is True   # 0.1 + 0.9 = 1.0 token exactly
    assert rl.allow(10) is False

    rl.set_limit("pro", 3)
    assert [rl.allow(0, "pro") for _ in range(4)] == [True, True, True, False]

hiddenTests.name: test_long_run_rate
hiddenTests.description: Bursts are bounded: the long-run rate stays at limit per window.
hiddenTests.code:
def test_long_run_rate():
    rl = RateLimiter(limit=5, window=10, mode="token_bucket", burst=5)
    accepted = sum(rl.allow(t) for t in range(0, 10_000) for _ in range(3))
    # 12 while the full bucket drains (t=0..4), then one every 2 seconds (t=6, 8, ...).
    assert accepted == 12 + 4997

hints: Each user's state is now just a token count and the last time you refilled it.
On each request: add `limit * elapsed / window` tokens, cap at `limit + burst`, then try to take one. With `Fraction` the arithmetic stays exact.
Three algorithms now share one interface. Pulling each into a small strategy class with `allow(user_id, limit, now)` keeps `RateLimiter` simple.

solution.explanation:
The token bucket stores `(tokens, last_refill)` per user and refills lazily on each
request with exact `Fraction` math, capped at `limit + burst`. With three algorithms,
the refactor is to pull each into a strategy object with a common
`allow(user_id, limit, now)` method and pick one in the constructor. Per-user limits
stay in `RateLimiter`, and every earlier mode keeps its exact behavior.
